sources.appraisal: Abstract, Results, first comparison: the pooled change in 1RM favored periodized over constant programs (ES 0.31, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.57). The trained undulating-versus-linear subgroup interval reached zero at reported precision. Trial durations, allocation bias and updated tables need full-text review. The authors favor undulation in trained lifters. A specific block sequence remains untested here.

sources.rights: CC BY (Europe PMC license record). Catalog use limited to metadata, links and original factual summaries.
sources.appraisal: Twenty-four recreational runners finished three baseline, two overload and one recovery week. Eight were classified as overreached and twelve as responders. Four unclassified finishers and eight dropouts limit generalization. Readiness contributed to classification.

claims.assertion: The heavy multiset group training at least three days per week gained more strength than the inactive group in the network estimate.
claims.limitations: Load was at least 80% of 1RM. Athletes were excluded. This control contrast cannot choose a starting load or a weekly set increase.
claims.assessment: Moderate to high within-study bias and indirect comparisons limit confidence. Few active prescriptions were clearly distinguishable.

support.result: Posterior standardized mean difference 1.60 (95% credible interval 1.38 to 1.82).
support.restriction: Network estimate for strength at trial end.

claims.assertion: Across the pooled adult samples, the average maximal-strength change under concurrent training was close to that under strength training alone.
claims.limitations: The maximal-strength analysis included 37 studies. Endurance mode and training status vary. A trained lower-body subgroup warrants separate consideration.
claims.assessment: Mean PEDro score 4.3/10 across included studies. The pooled interval accommodates a small reduction. Equivalence was not tested.

support.restriction: Maximal strength only. Explosive strength is a separate endpoint.

claims.assertion: In the trained subgroup, adding endurance training was associated with smaller gains on squat or leg-press 1RM.
claims.limitations: Running or cycling at greater than 70% of maximum heart rate at least twice weekly. Transfer to easy running, elite athletes and presses is uncertain.
claims.assessment: Small samples, short studies and nonrandomized comparisons weaken the subgroup inference. Training status was classified across studies.

support.result: Standardized effect −0.35 (95% CI −0.59 to −0.11) for concurrent versus resistance alone.
support.restriction: Six to 21 weeks is the range for included studies overall.

claims.assertion: Several athlete-reported well-being measures worsened during an acute increase in training load.
claims.limitations: Acute periods varied by study. Subjective reports can reflect other stressors. The review did not compare deload decisions.
claims.assessment: Heterogeneous protocols and instruments. Review-specific bias weights and categorical synthesis limit precision.

support.locator: Results, Table 7, acute increase in training load column and accompanying first result sentence
support.result: Review rated evidence for impairment moderate to strong on 13 subjective measures.
support.restriction: Count of measures, not independent trials. No common effect estimate.

claims.assertion: Change in nocturnal heart rate from baseline to the second overload week differed between the overreached and responder groups.
claims.limitations: The weekly summary does not establish how to interpret one night's reading or whether changing a session improves recovery.
claims.assessment: Small subgroup comparison with classification based on performance and subjective readiness. No prospective validation of an individual decision threshold.

support.locator: Results §3.3, Figure 3C, baseline to OL2 between-group contrast
support.result: Nocturnal HR rose in the overreached group and fell in responders (between-group change p = 0.002).
support.restriction: Direction describes group means. Neither within-group HR change reached significance.

relations.subject: trained-lower-body-strength@1
relations.reason: The trained squat/leg-press estimate narrows the mixed-population result. Both reviews include Robineau et al. (2016). Their pooled estimates answer different questions and share trials.
